title: RAD_SA.2.t
desc:
Хотя Финал выжег большую часть Земли, небеса над головой остались такими же нетронутыми, как и всегда. Звезды мерцали в великом запределье, придавая миру прекрасный вид чуда ночью, даже когда цивилизация догорала под ночным небом. Действительно, когда огни Земли погасли, небеса стали только ярче по сравнению с ними, и впервые за многие десятилетия все великолепие космоса можно было увидеть из любой точки мира.

Со временем человек снова обратил свое внимание на звезды, сначала пристально вглядываясь, затем удивляясь и, наконец, совершенствуясь. Люди восстановили древние линзы или сконструировали их сами и начали составлять карты небес. В своих наблюдениях они начали замечать, что некоторые звезды, казалось, блуждали по небу, как космические путешественники, направляющиеся в неизвестные небесные края. Для них существовало слово, хотя оно было утеряно во время Финала, поэтому люди просто стали называть их Странниками.

В землях Анд один звездочет влюбился в одного из этих странников. Там, где другие лениво дрейфовали по небесам, этот проносился по небу много раз за ночь. Он устанавливал свой дальногляд сразу после захода солнца, чтобы наблюдать за его прохождением, размышляя о его природе и назначении. Была ли это какая-то меньшая луна, подобная той, что тоже смотрела на него сверху вниз почти каждую ночь? Была ли это просто еще одна звезда, наделенная неестественной скоростью какой-то божественной или, возможно, сверхъестественной силой? Был ли это ангел? Бог, наблюдающий за своей паствой?

Однажды ночью он получил свой ответ. Наблюдая, как его "Странник" поднимается на гребень горизонта, он с ужасом увидел, что он охвачен пламенем, его след невероятно быстр и приближается. Разлетевшись на множество горящих осколков, он с оглушительным грохотом обрушился на близлежащие горы. Мчась к месту столкновения, звездочет с благоговением взирал на странное и удивительное зрелище перед ним. Странник не был естественным объектом - это было божественное творение! Обломки комнат, проходов и непонятных инструментов были очевидны в его форме, но самой большой находкой была не сама конструкция. Они лежал внутри - скелетообразные останки небесного существа.

title: RAD_SA.3.t
desc:
Инструктор читал лекцию, используя старую потрепанную, изношенную классную доску. Это было единственное, что было у сообщества - каждая царапина, которую нельзя было закрасить, была невосполнимой утратой. Тот факт, что его благодетелями были члены боевого комитета, доказал, насколько вожди племен доверяют человеку, известному как Команданте Энракес.

Говорили, что этот таинственный человек явился племени вскоре после того, как далекие взрывы уничтожили города, лежащие за джунглями. Поначалу он столкнулся с недоверием со стороны общества, но он быстро доказал свои способности, продемонстрировав племени некоторые новые приемы. Он принес с собой огромное количество изобретений и знаний - слов, которые достаточно заинтриговали вождей племен, чтобы удержать его рядом. Тот факт, что ему удалось внедриться в племя, обучая их этой новообретенной тактике, был не чем иным, как чудом. И все же некоторые говорили, что он был человеком чудес. Некоторые из наиболее мистических Старейшин шептались, что он был подарком для племени от высшей силы. Кем бы он ни был, он, безусловно, был полезен теперь, когда джунгли стали домом для различных враждебных чужаков, которые желали племени зла.

"Работа бойца никогда не прекращается, пока враг не отступит", - сказал Команданте молодежи, сгрудившейся вокруг него... "Ваша работа затяжная, и именно благодаря вашей работе вы станете известны как партизан. Вы придете к пониманию этого термина по мере того, как мы будем продвигаться в вашем обучении. А пока я продемонстрирую основные боевые движения. А теперь... внимательно наблюдайте."

Молодые мужчины и женщины были очарованы Энракесом и его работой. Он не прилагал никаких усилий в своей работе и ясно описал, чего он хочет от молодежи. Может быть, он все-таки был даром - он дал этому некогда изолированному сообществу шанс выжить в этом постоянно меняющемся мире. Можно было только гадать о его мотивах, но племя все равно было благодарно. Разве не было сказано, что слабые принимают ту помощь, которую им предлагают? Любого потенциального агрессора наверняка ждал бы сюрприз, если бы он встретился с человеком по имени Энракес и его новым отрядом бойцов.

title: RAD_SA.4.t
desc:
В городе Дежанейро, где ноги Спасителя коснулись вершины Монкорвокадо, проходил фестиваль, прямо у ног Спасителя. По всей длине проспекта Лоун-Хед выстроились разноцветные платформы, сопровождаемые мужчинами и женщинами в экзотических платьях, исполняющими хорошо срежиссированные танцы. Музыканты исполняли разнообразные популярные песни, маршируя рядом с танцорами. Торговцы доставляли свою еду и питье десятитысячному населению города, собравшемуся на этой единственной полоске старой, потрескавшейся дороги.

По их словам, это была традиция, которую город почитал за века до Судного дня. Праздник в честь бога, который наблюдал за ее жителями с самой высокой вершины города, широко раскинув руки, словно защищая ее и ее близких от вреда. Однако большая часть города не избежала Его очищающего пламени, и долгое время их традиция проводилась у статуи бога среди многочисленных руин города.

В конце концов раны Деджанарио зажили. Те, кто выжил, вышли вперед и вздохнули с облегчением после конца Приговора. Когда город начал медленно возвращаться к нормальной жизни, его лидеры, такие как король Момо Тридцатый, также начали восстанавливать то, что он потерял: дороги, налоги, водопровод... и древний праздник под названием Карнавал.

Обычаи и церемонии меняют форму и приспосабливаются под давлением времени. То, что когда-то было праздником для бога, стало праздником для города - праздником в честь того, что было потеряно, и празднованием наступления лучшего будущего. Ужасное прошлое осталось позади в Дежанейро, и с песнями, выпивкой и смехом десять тысяч объявляют о будущем, крича как один:

options.name: "Мы любим роскошь, только священники любят бедность!"
options.text: "Мы любим роскошь, только священники любят бедность!"

description:
В городе Дежанейро, где ноги Спасителя коснулись вершины Монкорвокадо, проходил фестиваль, прямо у ног Спасителя. По всей длине проспекта Лоун-Хед выстроились разноцветные платформы, сопровождаемые мужчинами и женщинами в экзотических платьях, исполняющими хорошо срежиссированные танцы. Музыканты исполняли разнообразные популярные песни, маршируя рядом с танцорами. Торговцы доставляли свою еду и питье десятитысячному населению города, собравшемуся на этой единственной полоске старой, потрескавшейся дороги.

title: RAD_SA.5.t
desc:
Никто в деревне больше не называл его по имени, просто "Эль Ультимо". Последний. После смерти Дуана Рамиреса двенадцать лет назад он стал единственным человеком в деревне, который знал, какой была жизнь до Великой войны. Хотя он родился и вырос в деревне, в молодости он несколько раз покидал ее. Всякий раз, когда дети спрашивали, он всегда рассказывал о городах, которые он посетил: Оахака, Керетаро, Веракрус, он мог часами описывать достопримечательности маленькой Ниаос. Но их любимой историей была история о том, как он поехал в Сьюдад-де-Мексико, и его отец купил ему мороженое у уличного торговца. Это была история, которая всегда выводила детей из себя, и они до поздней ночи засыпали его вопросами: каково это на вкус? Как им удавалось сохранять его таким холодным? У тебя все еще есть обертка?

Но дети больше не услышат его историй. Эль Ультимо скончался прошлой ночью во сне. Его многочисленные друзья и родственники собрались в его доме, устроив поминки по нему в его маленькой гостиной. Хотя они знали, что он прожил долгую и счастливую жизнь, они не могли избавиться от ощущения, что в его кончине было что-то важное и уникально трагичное.

title: RAD_SA.6.t
desc:
Многие из тех, кто сделал глупый выбор отправиться в плавание с экспедицией капитана Биссоннетта, отчаялись когда-либо добраться до места назначения. Дома это звучало так здорово, когда он потчевал их легендами о стране, избежавшей бомбежек, о "Тропическом Париже", как он его называл, который не тронуло пламя войны. Это был город в центре целого континента, который никто не ненавидел настолько, чтобы разрушать, и если люди придут с Биссонеттом, этот город станет их добычей.

После трудного путешествия они достигли тропического берега. Медленно пробираясь сквозь джунгли, экспедиционеры пробили себе путь вверх по великой реке. Они добрались до небольшого полуразрушенного поселения Сан-Тартар. Немногие оставшиеся в этом месте жители сигнализировали на языке, который частично понимал товарищ по кораблю из земель, когда-то известных как Иберия, что великий затерянный город, который они искали, находится далеко впереди. Поэтому экспедиционеры продвигались вперед, борясь по пути с течениями и ужасными тропическими болезнями. На протяжении многих миль единственным, что удерживало людей от поворота назад, был страх, что обратный путь будет длиннее, чем путь вперед. Однако, после всех трудов и имея в запасе всего четверть от их первоначальной экспедиции, они сделали это.

Это было прекрасно. Город был далеко не переполнен, но в поле зрения не было ни одной развалины. Земля была покрыта зеленью пальм, и толпы людей собирались, чтобы встретить незнакомцев, прибывающих на их берег. Сбитых с толку и измученных экспедиционеров приняли с распростертыми объятиями, и вскоре после их прибытия был устроен большой пир.

Они пришли в это место, в Дом Людей, в поисках добычи, чтобы забрать ее домой. К их шоку, то, что они искали, было дано им бесплатно. Тогда они поняли, что им не нужно брать то, что они нашли дома, потому что они нашли новый дом.

Экспедиционеры решили, вместо того чтобы приходить и разрушать город лучше остаться и помочь городу. В конце концов, кому захочется покидать рай?

title: RAD_SA.7.t
desc:
С Конца Времен бесчисленные сотни людей на этой земле погибли напрасно из-за эгоистичных устремлений эгоистичных людей. Семьи убиты, города сожжены, братья убивают братьев - и ради чего? Конфликт интересов? Затаённые обиды? Мало кто понимал причину насилия, поскольку целое поколение было втянуто в мир набегов и убийств в бессмысленной войне между двумя поселениями.

Однако, по мере того, как сменялось одно поколение и к власти приходило новое поколение, недовольное конфликтами, эпоха войны начала уступать место эпохе оттепели. Налеты прекратились, и количество смертей почти приблизилось к нулю. С этим налаживанием отношений наступила новая эра роста. Фермерам больше не нужно было бояться за свой урожай. Торговцам больше не нужно было принимать обширные и дорогостоящие меры защиты, чтобы обеспечить свою безопасность в путешествиях.

После долгих усилий два поселения стали еще ближе. Конфликт прекратился, поскольку узы между этими давно разлученными братьями начали укрепляться. Узы превратились в официальные связи, поскольку руководящие органы поселений продолжали интегрировать свои общества.

И с помощью рукопожатия была образована конфедерация. Объединение поселений под одной целью. Те, кто когда-то был так вовлечен в конфликт, теперь объединились в качестве партнеров в союзе. Их конфедерация стала бы образцом для многих, поскольку другие стремились принять участие в доброжелательном союзе городов. По мере того, как союз рос и его границы расширялись далеко за пределы двух поселений, узы между братьями и сестрами двух городов становились все крепче, и даже долгий ход времени не мог разорвать узы между ними.

title: Is There Anyone Out There?
desc:
"To anyone listening, please send help. We are trapped within the Mambu Apartment Complex in Marsilac, São Paulo. I am here with my wife, our sons and daughters, and our neighbor's children. We haven't eaten in days. One of the kids tried collecting the rainwater but is now sick, constantly vomiting. We are in dire need of assistance. I don't know how much longer we can..."

Click,

"Do not go to the Planalto. Me and a few friends thought the President had a secret bunker there, so did a bunch of people, and so did the military. They gunned us down before we could even speak. I got out... but they winged me. There's so much blood. If someone is near..."

Click.

"Sergeant always raved about the Americans this and the Americans that, a perfect race. Well, Sergeant, you're rotting in a ditch full of our bullets, and where are the Americans to help us? You'd think even the Japanese would have come by now. Unless... dear God. Could the exchange have spread that far? If this is everywhere, no, it can't be..."

Click.

"We are in a state of emergency. Do not leave your homes. Stay inside and await further instructions. We are in a state of emergency. Do not leave your homes. Stay inside and await further instructions. We are in a stage of emergency..."

title: Земля Свободы
desc:
Когда Жоао Амазонас унес революцию в далекие бразильские джунгли, большинство сочло его безумцем, и одним из его самых яростных критиков был Луис Карлос Престес. Когда началась война, Престес поддержал военные усилия бразильского правительства, тогда как Амазонас и его последователи продолжали уходить вглубь страны. Когда рухнули бомбы, Амазонас выжил, а Престес и его партия сгорели в ядерном огне.

Капитализм уничтожил сам себя - неизбежность, ставшая реальностью. Пока большинство оплакивало потерянное прошлое, перед другими открывалось смелое новое будущее, в котором для коммунизма не осталось никаких преград.

Они спустились в пепел, закаленные и уверенные в своей миссии. Какими бы кровожадными ни были капиталисты, они не сочли нужным сжигать джунгли, где жили лишь пару тысяч, в отличие от городов, которые оказались стерты с лица земли. И когда измученные, голодные, заброшенные люди искали спасения, их избавителями стали эти новые миссионеры.

Под пристальным взглядом Жоао Амазонаса ряды Коммунистической партии Бразилии быстро росли. Пусть плоды их труда были скудны, опустошены радиацией и ее последствиями, но теперь они полностью принадлежали лишь им самим. Для многих этого было достаточно - свобода в бедности лучше рабства в изобилии.

Сегодня коммунистическое движение пока лишь тонкий ручей, но вскоре оно превратится в бурный поток. Капитализм потерпел крах - его последним наследием остались лишь руины. Мир будущего не будет строиться на этих обломках. Настоящее изменится и уйдет, а вместе с ним придет и коммунизм.

description:
Когда Жоао Амазонас унес революцию в далекие бразильские джунгли, большинство сочло его безумцем, и одним из его самых яростных критиков был Луис Карлос Престес. Когда началась война, Престес поддержал военные усилия бразильского правительства, тогда как Амазонас и его последователи продолжали уходить вглубь страны. Когда рухнули бомбы, Амазонас выжил, а Престес и его партия сгорели в ядерном огне.

Капитализм уничтожил сам себя - неизбежность, ставшая реальностью. Пока большинство оплакивало потерянное прошлое, перед другими открывалось смелое новое будущее, в котором для коммунизма не осталось никаких преград.

Они спустились в пепел, закаленные и уверенные в своей миссии. Какими бы кровожадными ни были капиталисты, они не сочли нужным сжигать джунгли, где жили лишь пару тысяч, в отличие от городов, которые оказались стерты с лица земли. И когда измученные, голодные, заброшенные люди искали спасения, их избавителями стали эти новые миссионеры.

Под пристальным взглядом Жоао Амазонаса ряды Коммунистической партии Бразилии быстро росли. Пусть плоды их труда были скудны, опустошены радиацией и ее последствиями, но теперь они полностью принадлежали лишь им самим. Для многих этого было достаточно - свобода в бедности лучше рабства в изобилии.

Сегодня коммунистическое движение пока лишь тонкий ручей, но вскоре оно превратится в бурный поток. Капитализм потерпел крах - его последним наследием остались лишь руины. Мир будущего не будет строиться на этих обломках. Настоящее изменится и уйдет, а вместе с ним придет и коммунизм.

title: For Another Thousand Years
desc:
A hand outstretched pointing to a smoke trail in the sky, a white line crossing the pale blue, then another, and another. A daytime of shooting stars. The next day the streaks had passed and the sky had returned to its blue. The days remained quiet. Those outsiders who would make sojourns into their jungle the noise they would bring ceased. It was not unusual for days or even weeks to go by without contact between the Yaminawa tribe and those interlopers but as weeks stretched into months the quiet became unusual. The roads they had once used were taken over by the noise of nature. The tribe lived as they had for generations before. The new ways became old ways and passed out of mind. The interlopers passed from truth, to memory and into fable as a decade passed since the smoke in the sky.

Two children raised on the fables ran along the bank of a stream. That day they heard rustling from the undergrowth. One wonders if it was a boar, or a snake. One jokes that it may be one of the old interlopers, come to reclaim their lands now overgrown. To rebuild the fences that nature and the tribe had since torn down. From the undergrowth emerged a man. Blinded and scarred, stumbling around trying to find his way. Reduced to an animal. The children ran and so the tale of the interloper stumbling around as a beast by the side of a stream was added to the memory and passed into the fables they would tell their children. It would be another generation before another interloper would find their way to the tribe to add to the coiled fables and bring them back from memory into truth.

title: One in a Million
desc:
Five. The Manaus skyline, alight from the wafting blazes of riots and police muzzle flashes amidst blaring sirens, gained a new feature: a small bright light in the southern direction, across the river. I blinked, and it got bigger. Four. I jolted back as a stray pellet hit my office window; the police in the port must be losing control. The light grows larger. Three. The light fades, its figure reduced to a black object trailing towards the city against the Amazonian sunset. Two. The gunfire stops. For just one moment, the whole city seems silent, our eyes drawn towards it – we are granted fractions of a second to reflect on our existence. I close my eyes.

One. A splash, followed by a thud in the riverbed. The police and rioters portside look on for a few moments in silence, unaware of the miracle they just witnessed. Riots resume.

In the following 12 hours, the city of Manaus stopped receiving all communications from other major metropolitan areas in Brazil, an unscathed oasis in the new, nuclear reality. Riots continued, hundreds lay dead on the streets, though the Police would eventually gain control, and a shoot-on-sight curfew was instituted to halt the massive exodus of people and resources from the city, its residents unaware there was nowhere else to go amidst the city-imposed information blackout.

I knew everything I needed, however. Away from prying eyes in the dead of night, I grab my wetsuit and venture into the River Negro, flashlight in hand. Wading through the water at low tide, the reflection of the flashlight off the warhead hits my eye, and I reach out and touch it.

title: Рио: День ноль
desc:
Пальцы Франсишки дрожали и не слушались, пока она пыталась набрать заветный номер. Ошибка. Быстро повесила трубку, снова сняла и попробовала еще раз. Звонок не прошел. Франсишка повесила трубку, сняла ее и набрала номер в третий раз. Гудки.

"Мамочка! Мне страшно!" - всхлипнула Витория. Франсишка с облегчением вздохнула.

"Дорогая, пожалуйста, слушай. Времени мало. Ты далеко, ты в безопасности. Ты умная, сообразительная, у тебя все получится. И запомни: я и вся наша семья тебя очень любим."

"Мамочка, пожалуйста..."

"Я читала об этом в книге. Прячься в подвале семь дней - за это время радиация ослабнет. Всегда кипяти воду, чтобы избежать болезней. Капля отбеливателя убивает бактерии. Если вода заражена, сначала очисти ее активированным углем. Вода очень важна, запомни..."

Вспышка - ослепительная, ярче всего, что когда-либо видели. Франсишка ахнула, телефон выскользнул из рук. Мир погрузился в кромешную тьму - она смотрела прямо в сторону ядерного взрыва. Электромагнитный импульс уничтожил все, что было связано с электричеством.

В доме закричала другая ее дочь. Франсишка упала на пол, на четвереньках пробираясь к детям. Наткнулась на стол, споткнулась, но все же нашла их. "Все будет хорошо," - солгала она, протягивая руки, чтобы прижать детей к себе. Они сжались вокруг матери, дрожа, а она тихо напевала колыбельную.

Еще одна вспышка. Взрывная волна разнесла стекла, бетон рушился, металл скрежетал, и Рио обрушился вокруг них.

title: Буэнос-Айрес: День ноль
desc:
Рауль никогда не был особо религиозным человеком, хотя был окружен учением Христа с самого детства. Его отец не раз предостерегал: заботься о своей душе, ибо настанет день, когда человечество предстанет перед Божьим судом. И тогда лишь его собственные поступки решат, будет ли он вознесен в рай или обречен блуждать по пустому, оставленному Богом миру.

Когда Рауль поднял взгляд и увидел, как вдалеке над горизонтом поднимается зловещее грибовидное облако, а в его ушах звенели истошные крики всего Буэнос-Айреса, он понял, каким же он был глупцом.

Второе пришествие свершилось. И с чем он предстанет перед Страшным судом?

Кадры прошлого пронеслись перед его глазами. Упав на колени, Рауль превратился в недвижимую фигуру пока окружавшая его толпа куда-то отчаянно бежала. В его сознании мелькали образы - наркотики, алкоголь, женщины. Осколки жизни, прожитой в грехе. Какой в этом всем был смысл? Что скажет он в свое оправдание, представ перед святым Петром?

Сирены гремели, как семь труб Апокалипсиса. Рауль сложил руки, как его учили в детстве, и впервые за многие годы обратился к Богу.

Его молитва была беззвучной, едва слышной. Она предназначалась лишь одному. Мольба о прощении перед лицом неминуемой гибели. И когда все, что было у него на душе, оказалось сказано, он остался на месте, надеясь, что этого слабого подношения хватит, чтобы искупить всю его прежнюю жизнь.

Рауль закрыл глаза и стал ждать ослепительного пламени, что заберет его из этого мира.

title: Бразилиа: День ноль
desc:
Когда София была маленькой, бабушка читала ей отрывки из Библии о Вознесении, Апокалипсисе и конце времен. Повзрослев, она отошла от христианства и страшных образов огня и серы - особенно после того, как поняла, что ее образ жизни, как говорила мама, считается греховным. Но теперь, стоя на верхнем этаже Конгресса и наблюдая, как весь город пылает в пламени, она не могла не вспомнить те слова.

Горели почти все здания, кроме Конгресса. На улицах открыто дрались люди. Они врывались в магазины, хватая все, что могли найти. В воздухе смешался едкий запах дыма с химическим смрадом обгоревших тел.

Она и сама не знала, почему пришла именно сюда, в самую гущу бури. Возможно, это была тщетная попытка сохранить хотя бы иллюзию нормальности. Возможно, надежда обрести хоть какое-то спасение.

А может, она просто устала бежать.

Всю свою жизнь София Уолтер бежала от своей страны. Ее родина хотела сломать ее, вырвать из нее все человеческое, заменив чем-то пустым. И потому София бежала через океан, в новую жизнь - новую страну, новый язык, новый шанс. Но даже это оказалось недолговечным.

В небе мелькнуло нечто, устремляясь прямо к зданию. Оно прочертило небосвод, подобно молнии из древних мифов. Немецкая ракета. Конец все-таки настал. София раскинула руки, готовясь встретить неизбежное, и впервые за долгие годы помолилась - о том, что если жизнь после смерти все-таки существует, она была лучше.

options.name: А затем, с ослепительной вспышкой, не осталось ничего.

title: Сан-Паулу: День седьмой
desc:
"Этот район находится под защитой Партии социального прогресса," - разносился по улицам голос из громкоговорителей на закопченном грузовике. - "Граждане должны оставаться в своих домах ради собственной безопасности." - В уцелевших зданиях бледные руки осторожно раздвигали шторы и жалюзи, освобождая место для пустых глаз, следящих за проезжающей машиной.

"Мародеры и бездельники будут расстреляны." - Грузовик медленно проползал мимо фонарного столба, на котором покачивалось скрюченное в безветренном воздухе тело. На его шее висела картонка из-под пиццы с надписью ГРАБИТЕЛЬ. Машина напоминала огромного, тяжело дышащего зверя, готового в любой момент разродиться тремя вооруженными милиционерами при первом признаке угрозы - или добычи.

Плакаты с изображением президента Адемара обозначали подконтрольную территорию. Хотя с момента войны его никто не видел и не слышал, любые слухи о его смерти мгновенно подавлялись. Именно его воля и авторитет позволяли Партии социального прогресса удерживать контроль над этим районом, защищая его от разрастающихся банд.

Те, у кого был выбор, склонялись под знамя ПСП, видя в нем остатки былой стабильности. Со временем плакаты выцветут и покроются трещинами, а военачальник Аде Бар войдет в историю уже совсем по другой причине - но до этого пройдут долгие десятилетия, а здесь никто никогда не думал дальше завтрашнего дня.

Еще дальше вглубь улицы патрулировали отряды милиции, закутанные в тяжелые куртки, скрывая лица за противогазами. На поясах щелкали счетчики Гейгера, стрекоча, как цикады. Те, кто находился под их "защитой", ютились в своих домах, подставляя ведра под капающую из ржавых труб мутную воду; ворочаясь в импровизированных клиниках, с трудом хватая отравленный радиацией воздух. description:
"Этот район находится под защитой Партии социального прогресса," - разносился по улицам голос из громкоговорителей на закопченном грузовике. - "Граждане должны оставаться в своих домах ради собственной безопасности." - В уцелевших зданиях бледные руки осторожно раздвигали шторы и жалюзи, освобождая место для пустых глаз, следящих за проезжающей машиной.

"Мародеры и бездельники будут расстреляны." - Грузовик медленно проползал мимо фонарного столба, на котором покачивалось скрюченное в безветренном воздухе тело. На его шее висела картонка из-под пиццы с надписью ГРАБИТЕЛЬ. Машина напоминала огромного, тяжело дышащего зверя, готового в любой момент разродиться тремя вооруженными милиционерами при первом признаке угрозы - или добычи.

Плакаты с изображением президента Адемара обозначали подконтрольную территорию. Хотя с момента войны его никто не видел и не слышал, любые слухи о его смерти мгновенно подавлялись. Именно его воля и авторитет позволяли Партии социального прогресса удерживать контроль над этим районом, защищая его от разрастающихся банд.

Те, у кого был выбор, склонялись под знамя ПСП, видя в нем остатки былой стабильности. Со временем плакаты выцветут и покроются трещинами, а военачальник Аде Бар войдет в историю уже совсем по другой причине - но до этого пройдут долгие десятилетия, а здесь никто никогда не думал дальше завтрашнего дня.

title: The Long Winter
desc:
Cold. Hungry. Tired. Weak. These were the only thoughts circling Beatriz's head as she felt the radiation chip away at what little energy she had left. She had lived her life with the ever-present, dangling threat of the bomb over her head, but had never expected all the boasts and jeers hurled across the Atlantic to ever amount to anything, nor did she suspect it'd leave her like this. She was empty, she was weak - and her family was dying.

Or so she'd thought. As she felt her old bones finally begin to give in, and her eyes slowly shut with exhaustion - something just barely visible over the horizon shocked her to her core. People. A well-armed group of men were patrolling the city's ruins, bags and knapsacks filled to the brim with what loot they could scavenge. Some of it would be used, some traded - but all necessary. The group patrolled the streets solemnly, taking moments of silence in between their looting, as some form of solidarity with those lost. Perhaps they could help her - perhaps they could help her family?

They slowly made their march through the gutted remains of the city, picking apart what little it still had to offer, like desperate vultures to a rotting corpse, before finally reaching Beatriz. None of them particularly knew what to say at first, looking at her fragile, radiation-worn body like she was an anomaly. Small mutters of 'What do we do with her?', and 'We can't leave her like this.' were all Beatriz could pick up, until, suddenly the de facto leader put his foot down with a sigh.

"Boys, we're going."

That was all he had to say. Beatriz was shocked. She begged and pleaded for something - anything to alleviate her, and her children's suffering - if even only for a moment. But the group picked up momentum all the same, as if they couldn't hear her. She seized what little energy she had left and quickly snatched at the nearest ankle, in some vain, desperate attempt to draw what little sympathy could be offered. But all she was rewarded with was a swift kick, throwing her to the ground, leaving her recoiling in pain.

Beatriz gazed at the men walking off, cursing them with all her might until her lungs could draw no more breath. 'Murderers! Savages! Bastards!' But it was all for nought, they continued down the path all the same, and Beatriz could do nothing but sit there, feeling herself slip away into the abyss further.

title: The Last General
desc:
It had been 35 days since the world had been shaken to its core. 35 days of radiation sickness, 35 days of looting, and 35 days of suffering. But General Gabriel cared not, after all, he was the president now, and presidents had much more important matters to deal with.

His commands were simple, at least in his mind. He barked a passionate rant about how that 'traitorous bastard' on the other side of the hill had damaged the 'sanctity' of his 'glorious new Republic' by proclaiming himself to be the 'true president', and how all the 'loyal soldiers' stationed in this bunker would 'save Brazil', and bring it to 'greater heights than any president could!'' But that meant nothing to the rest of his squad. They were tired, hungry - and above all else, they wanted to go home - what was left of it at least.

"Men, you may not know it now, but I am proud of you. By my side, we'll finally reclaim what that turncoat took from us! You, my friends, are the last true patriots of Brazil! Now come - under my genius, we shall reclaim what is ours!'

The soldiers reluctantly picked up their rifles, knowing there was no alternative, and began to file out of the bunker until - suddenly, a single shot echoed through the room, finding a spot behind Gabriel's bandages, and into his skull. The room fell silent, as the identity of the shooter was on everyone's mind. Who had been brave enough to take out the mad 'president'?

But that silence was soon shattered. "Men." one of the NCO's started to say, making his way to the front of the room. "I care not what you do from this point onwards. You can stay here, you can make your ways home, or you may choose to follow me. But just know that I could no longer sit idly by and watch that madman throw away our lives like that. Our best chance of survival is working together, and no matter what any of you may say - I can tell you all feel the same."

The bunker quickly became abuzz with shocked conversation as soon as he finished, the soldiers wondering what they were going to do, or what they could do. However, all that mattered to them was after that grueling month, the choice was finally theirs to make.

title: The First Harvest
desc:
Agriculture was never easy, not least since the bombs fell. The farms that had once grown marvelous harvests had now become nothing more than hollow shells of what their pasts, soil that was once renowned for growing coffee beans and wheat aplenty now left as a sad relic of life before the bombs. Many had given up hope by this point, assuming there was nothing left for them, but there were still some determined enough to find a way, no matter what it took.

Though that wasn't to say it was easy. Without the convenience awarded through mechanization, farming was now a much more arduous task, the use of impromptu equipment becoming commonplace - jobs once easily done by a handful of people now taking the effort of the community. But that didn't matter to them - surviving did, they still pushed through, diligently tilling the soil, day in, day out, praying that something, anything, would answer their prayers.

Once the harvest had arrived, there was little fanfare, in part due to apathy - and in part due to disappointment. Where many had expected at least enough to survive, there was nothing. Most crops had died to exposure, becoming shriveled and inedible. Those that hadn't immediately to the conditions had a much more adverse reaction to it, instead mutating into mocking facsimiles of what they should've been, misshapen and bruised, spitting in the faces of the remaining few who had kept any hope.

At least that's what many thought. In between all the death and mutation was a single field, nestled right on the edge of town - a beacon for all who had intended to give up. Golden stalks of grain shooting high into the sky, gifts from the Lord himself!

The town erupted into whoops and cheers as they harvested the crop, it was enough grain to keep them fed through the autumn - hell, even the winter! The air was jubilant, many feeling something in their hearts they hadn't felt since the bombs fell - some not even before that - hope. The President-Mayor took a moment to himself once the celebrations had ceased, and thanked God for all he did. After all, such a miracle could be nothing short of divine intervention.

title: Wind Chill
desc:
As the world tumbled into a winter of its own, in the land of eternal winter four lonely men clung onto what remained. They counted 5 cans of food left. The shipments that brought them a stream of life giving nutrients would no longer come to their solitary port. The rest of their platoon had gradually succumbed to the elements. Yet still they marched with purpose clinging to the hope that at the main expedition post to the west they might find some faint signs of life. It would be a trivial journey; an hour by helicopter perhaps, four by boat, yet on foot through the snow it consumed their resolve. The cans counted down and so they returned to the means humans had clung to since the very beginning, hunting seals and penguins in hope of maintaining the energy to reach the distant meeting point. Gradually the heat left their limbs, as their hope began to dwindle, as the cold seeped into them.

After days of the unbroken white horizon they saw a black shape on the water's edge. At first they assumed it was some tent blown to the water's edge, then as it came into starker relief, a boat that must have been broken. It would be no use to them, left as flotsam from a bygone age. Yet as they reached it and examined the hull there were no holes to be found. Hope spread like fire through their limbs as they looked into the ship finally seeing an escape from the white hell, until they examined the fuel gauge and then the tank itself. It was empty. The last of the heat that drove their limbs forward left them and beside the boat they waited for the cold to embrace them in stillness. They were in the end interrupted, 5 Argentine soldiers stood surrounding them, surrounding the boat. Guns were raised on both sides; perhaps they would not find their oblivion in stillness but in the heat and fire that had torn the world apart. In the end however, the guns were lowered. The Argentines had with them fuel enough to fill the tanks. As the engine lit the combined platoon of nine men set sail, liberated from their doom, from the stillness that might have claimed them.

title: Adrift
desc:
For the kelpers of the Falkland Islands, the first sign of trouble came in the form of silence.

The isolated isles that sat on the edge of the world had remained in contact with the outside world largely via radio, and the sudden cessation of any sort of communication was certainly a call for concern, as tensions across the world had been brewing for months. When the lines went dead on one unassuming day, some figured it was a simple malfunction of equipment. The real story took weeks to arrive, in the form of Brazilian and Argentinian soldiers washing up on the shores. The soldiers, emaciated and suffering from radiation poisoning, offered harrowing tales of a thermonuclear war that had swept the planet. The Falklands was spared thanks to its strategic irrelevance, and as a result, had become one of the few places on Earth untouched by atomic fire.

For the next few centuries, the island would find itself swept into unfamiliar waters. The first winter was the most difficult, but was not as harsh as the most pessimistic assessments of nuclear winter suggested. Cut off from the global supply, food shortages wreaked havoc upon the island's inhabitants in those darkened days. Yet, once the kelpers had emerged from the other side, the Falklands became a bastion of tranquility as the rest of the world roiled in anarchy, subsisting largely from the ocean and pastures that had sustained them before the war.

This peace continued for hundreds of years uninterrupted, its inhabitants rarely paying any mind as to the state of the rest of the world. It had been lost, but the kelpers remained. Then, on one afternoon of clear skies, a ship arrived on their shores, its passengers offering wares from civilizations yet unheard of...

title: The New Matador
desc:
"Ladies and gentlemen," called out the barker, "hailing from the Western Realms, he is the favoured of the President-King, he is the slayer of a hundred men and a thousand beasts... he is the Matador!"

The Matador raised his sword and flowed out his cape in pre-emptive triumph, and the crowd that filled the stadium cheered him along. On the other side of the arena the cage opened, and the beastmasters scuttled away while his prey emerged. It was a fat thing, tall and yet stubby, with rubbery grey skin and a wide mouth. There were other foes that emerged from the wild cities, but the Matador found the hippo was the most challenging of them all. Something about their eyes, their gawping face; they were predators in the bodies of fools.

The hippo charged, drawn to the Matador's red cape. It was fast, but the Matador stepped away from its stampede, bringing his sword low and driving it into its flank. The pained cry of the hippo could not escape the crowd's cheer. It stumbled and thrashed about, trying to swing itself towards the Matador, but he danced past. He slashed the beast's right foreleg, and heard the tendon snap as the hippo went down.

His offsiders emerged behind them, armed with nets and knives. The hippo tried to raise itself up, but weighted nets piled atop it, weighing it down with each new item. It took eight of the heaviest nets they had, but they had held the beast down in but half a minute. As it struggled to raise itself up, the Matador approached it with his sword held high. He did not even blink as he struck the top of its head, shattering bone with a powerful chop.

title: Reunited Once More
desc:
It is said, in the histories, passed down through the years, that before the lives of a hundred generations, before the fall of the Suzerain and the rise of the Protectorate, before Ançera even existed, that there was a land. A land beyond the Great Ocean, split from ours by sea and storm. Once united, then divided by the Calamity. For most, they dismissed these stories as fiction. Tall tales from a world long past. But Manuel thought differently. When his grandmother told him the legends, of beaches made of gold, of continents made of ice, of a world beyond the pale, his heart knew it to be true.

He spent a year persuading the Lord Protector, another two overseeing the construction of a vessel fit for his mission, and, with one more year to gather a crew, he finally set sail. It was perilous. A far cry from the rivers of Ançera, the Great Ocean lived up to its name. Storm after storm rocked the ship, waves so high it could swallow a God, and waters so barren the crew had to eat their own boots to survive. With half of the crew dead, Manuel's First Mate begged him to turn back. To forsake this fantasy. Her request was denied, and so they pressed on. On and on, day after day, delirious and desperate they pushed through endless, empty sea.

Then they saw it. There were no golden beaches, no lands of ice and snow, no fantasies told by Manuel's Avó, but it was there. It was real. And so, eyes sunken, stomach empty, and skin coarse, Manuel cried out in joy as the two worlds became one once more.

title: Tomb Raider
desc:
Three figures, clad in dirty brown robes and each wearing a meticulously maintained gas mask, slowly walked through the ruins of an ancient city, named Sãopulo according to a faded sign on the outskirts. Collapsed spires of twisted steel, streets full of shattered glass, the detritus of a great civilization brought to ruin by its arrogance and hubris. One of the robed men carried a map, once used by tourists or drivers from distant lands and now nearly in tatters, but legible enough to find a path.

Among the red rust and blackened concrete, the green of plant life was starting to return: vines and grasses and stunted trees were clinging on, slowly overtaking the ruins. Packs of wild dogs roamed the streets, but they usually kept their distance, or were easy enough to scare off with shouts.

They made their way toward the center of the map, until they reached the spot that had been circled on it. It was a fancy building, or at least once was, but now could be full of treasure. And so the prospectors set to work.

It took two days of steady labor, but eventually they got into the building, and to a metal door inside. The locks that once held it had rusted away, so they were able to force it open. Inside was a room of death and mold; many skeletons and bones laid all around, surrounded by gold, paintings, electronics and other things once held to be valuable. The explorers walked past all of it, scouring the room until one exclaimed. They found it: books! While many had been ruined by age and water, many of the words were still legible! The three celebrated their discovery, but then all three bowed their heads, mumbled a prayer while stretching their arms in the air, then bowed to the piles of bones around them. Once the ritual was completed, they carefully gathered the books, and left, closing the metal door behind them to give the dead their final rest.

options.name: Knowledge is the greatest treasure of all.
options.text: Knowledge is the greatest treasure of all.

title: Искупитель
desc:
На вершине старого, изрытого трещинами холма, где давно уже не осталось ни зелени, ни жизни, стояла статуя. Вернее, то, что от нее осталось - полусломанная голова, лежащая дальше по склону, и фрагменты ног, все еще вросшие в камень.

Ее имя давно стерлось из людской памяти, но те, кто кое-как выживал поблизости, называли ее Искупителем. Никто не знал, откуда пошло это имя. Однако те, кто утверждали, что знают правду о Старом мире, говорили, что когда-то статуя возвышалась над процветающим городом, населенным миллионами людей. Что она была чем-то вроде стража - вечно наблюдавшего за теми, кто жил внизу.

А потом пришли бомбы.

Жизни в Со-По, как теперь называли пустошь, где когда-то стоял Искупитель, почти не осталось. Но те немногие, кто еще там обитал, порой приносили подножью разрушенной статуи подношения. Одни верили, что это божество, сумевшее пережить огненный апокалипсис. Другие просто хотели убедиться, что хоть что-то столь великое, как Искупитель из прошлого, могло уцелеть в новом мире.

Ветви, камни, личные безделушки - все это приносили к его ногам. А голова статуи безучастно взирала на путников и паломников, которые взбирались на холм, чтобы доверить ему свои дары.

Со временем это паломничество превратилось в ежегодный ритуал для тех, кто мог позволить себе столь опасное путешествие через руины Со-По. Среди таких преданных часто возникали споры - кем же был Искупитель?

Богом? Царем? Простым человеком? Что за существо могло вдохновить тех, кто был до нас, на создание столь величественного монумента в свою честь?

title: Between Two Worlds
desc:
From the balcony of his villa overlooking the canal, Halconero looked over the land that raised him to prominence. La Serenísima had risen from the carcass of a society that could shape the earth with ease and precision. Their restoration of its greatest work was crude—hundreds had died and millions had been spent to realise a tenth of its potential—but it had connected the two halves of the known world. In ten years, they built great fleets and sent them across the seas, and soon they became the world's premier trading hub.

"And you promise me a sight more beautiful than this?" Halconero turned to his seneschal, whose servants unfurled two flags atop his balcony's table. Halconero recognised the first flag from his studies. "Barry of thirteen argent and gules," he recited, "a quarter azure charged with fifty mullets argent." It had once belonged to an ancient and impossibly powerful empire; the captains and merchants of La Serenísima had found this old flag across the world. "And you found it here?"

"Locked in a chest, deep in the ruins of the old canal. My God, the implications..."

But the second flag eluded him. "Quarterly, first argent charged with mullet azure, second gules... This one's new."

"Not so new, Your Grace." Next to the flags was a leather-bound book, which he opened to a page bearing a similar flag. Beneath it was a brief description, describing it as a symbol often found near La Serenísima. Its proximity suggested a link with the canal and its surrounding demesne, but there had been no clear evidence.

Halconero stared at the flag for a long time. Then he turned, bowed to his seneschal. "Thank you, Arnau. Have the scribes record them in triplicate. Distribute them to the universities, and fold the originals somewhere safe in the treasury."

title: The Mountain Kings
desc:
"You have news from Olaroz, Your Majesty." The metal walls of Atacama's royal palace reverberated with the courtier's voice. Since their return to the surface, some suggested that a more fitting residence was made for the King, but his ancestors had already decided that matter. King Bernardo IV wasn't going to overrule them, not when they brought the Atacama so far.

"If it is anything less than an unconditional surrender, I will not be amused."

"He wishes to meet with you to discuss a tru-"

"Enough. That traitor wouldn't want to negotiate if he wasn't losing. We'll see if he comes around when our catapults start knocking on the doors of his tin palace." The rebel's head would serve quite well as a reminder. "Anything else for me?"

"Yes, Your Majesty. We received a letter from the Mapuche King of Valdivia. It is for your eyes only, Your Majesty. With tensions between us as high as they are, I wouldn't want lowborn intuition clouding your decision-making."

Bernardo opened the letter to an intoxicating scent, the smell of something innocent, something lost. Inside, the Mapuche King detailed a marriage proposal between one of his daughters and Bernardo. Such was romance these days, a game of politics, but one that could spare thousands. Were he bolder and younger, he would have said no, but as his beard grew whiter each day...

"Tell the King I am interested in his proposal, even willing to meet to discuss it. That will be all for today, thank you." The courtier dutifully nodded and left. His Majesty wondered if he was growing soft; what would they think of this? But ultimately, he knew he had to leave a legacy past a trail of severed heads and bones, something for King Bernardo V.

options.name: A good king knows how to balance fear and love.

title: Last Stand of the Gaucho
desc:
A gaucho atop his horse was atop this world, striding along it with both dignity in himself and command of his surroundings. Atop his horse, the gaucho rode across the snow-capped mountains and through the maize and tobacco fields, the appointed master and protector of the villages and the farms. They obeyed no masters save their God and their codes, and for a time they believed that was all that had been given to them. When news of the Paulistas first emerged, emerging like cockroaches from the metal graveyards the gauchos dared not tread into, their first reactions were a mixture of curiosity and fear. Their scouts were easy to dispatch; they had such little command of their own horses that the gauchos often took them as recompense for their frustrations. But news of the Paulistas continued to grow north of the Pelotas River, as did their ambitions and their patrols.

At the Monte Negro Canyon, the first expeditionary force of the Paulistas arrived in the early afternoon. They marched in three columns, a soft but steady war drum announcing their arrival. They wielded firearms longer than the hand pistols that the gauchos wore. At the head of the middle column flew the flag of Ad Baro, their patron saint of war and governance who was said to once rule this land. The first gauchos to intercept them threw their bolas into the columns. Their aim was true; the middle column, tangled up in leather cords, fell to the ground. But the Paulistas raised their guns, and plumes of smoke followed small lead pebbles that launched at the gauchos like an unruly bronco. The pebbles struck chests and limbs, throwing riders off their mounts.

Successive waves of gauchos fared little better. The Paulistas regrouped and stood their ground, merging their columns into squares that the gauchos could not break through, no matter how many arrows and bolas flew. They tried to dodge the lead, but they always moved quicker than the gauchos anticipated. The Battle of Monte Negro Canyon ended with the gauchos fleeing, as curious and fearful as when they first met the Paulistas.

title: Peace On The River
desc:
Once upon a time, there were two great kingdoms.

They were both alike in many ways, divided only by a mighty river. One was a nation of horse riders. Their steeds, both flesh and metal, battered the earth as they rode under the banner of the sun itself. The other, naming itself the Empire of the 'Paulistas' (an ancient title  - the meaning of which has been lost to time) held itself a nation of farmers.

The two kingdoms rarely got along. The horse-riders held the Paulistas as arrogant know-it-alls. The Paulistas held the horse-riders as boorish oafs. And as the years went by, these tensions grew alongside technology. The Paulistas found new and innovative ways to cultivate life whereas the horse-riders steeds became more metal than flesh.

The tensions kept growing. The vitriol became more and more spiteful. Until one terrible day, the two kingdoms realized that they possessed weapons capable of utterly obliterating the other from the face of the earth.

It was then that the rulers of these kingdoms thought back to the ivy-covered bunkers in the depths of the jungles. Of the ruined cities that still dotted the landscape and the glass deserts barren of all life. And they could only make one decision from there.

Upon a mighty ziggurat in front of a roaring crowd, a treaty was signed by the two leaders. One that would guarantee peace upon the river from now and forevermore. There would be trials, and tests, and barriers, but for that one singular moment, there would be peace. And the mistakes of the past would be just that.

title: RAD_EA.1.t
desc:
Когда пришел Конец, никто не счел нужным омывать склоны Гималаев адским пламенем. Хотя некоторые города и авиабазы в регионе испытали пламя, расчеты и стратегии генералов великих держав не видели особой пользы в выжигании отдаленных и бесполезных земель бесплодных гор. И поэтому склоны остались нетронутыми, ощущая только нежный солнечный поцелуй таких далеких термоядерных взрывов.

И со временем эти горы станут домом для могущественного королевства.

Народ этого королевства когда-то назывался "шерпа", народ востока. В мире, охваченном пламенем, никто не знал, что именно находится к востоку от них, так что название в конечном счете устарело. Когда-то они были разведчиками, кочевниками, торговцами, используя свой многовековой опыт работы в горах, чтобы зарабатывать на жизнь среди более оседлого народа. Именно эти навыки превратили бы их в правителей высот.

Не сдерживаемые старыми государствами, шерпы создали нацию, которая соединила две стороны Азии, разделенные великими горами, используя свои уникальные знания гор, чтобы направлять торговцев по непроходимой местности. Поскольку богатства из других новых королевств текли через их земли, шерпы стали доминирующей силой в горах, стимулируя торговлю и коммерцию по всему континенту. Их рынки стали самостоятельными силами, а затем конкурентами и, наконец, гигантами торговли, превосходящими всех их конкурентов.

У подножия Джомолангмы будет построена великая столица, которая укрепит власть людей гор. Со временем они перестанут быть известными как люди востока и примут имя, которым их назовет большинство завистливых народов. Теперь они были навсегда известны, как наампа - народ неба.

title: RAD_EA.2.t
desc:
В великой империи мореплавателей на Самом Дальнем Востоке высокими головами с каменными лицами украшают носы своих кораблей, внутренности своих зданий, алтари своих храмов и дворцов. У каждого человека есть свое имя для этих молчаливых идолов: Защитник, Те-Кто-Наблюдает, Арингара. Каким бы ни было прозвище, империя почитает их как своих богов-покровителей, ее духи-хранители приходят, чтобы защитить их из их райских обителей.

title: RAD_EA.3.t
desc:
Слуга стоял по стойке смирно вместе с тысячью товарищей на территории дворца. Старые знамена с хвалебными надписями по всей длине развевались на легком летнем ветерке. Все они были одеты в полные доспехи, катаны должным образом вложены в ножны, ожидая прибытия Его Величества.

Остров может быть разорван, перекован и снова разорван, но некоторые вещи созданы для того, чтобы оставаться там целую вечность. Больше, чем труд человеческих рук или их богатство, традиции и идеи сделаны из более прочного материала, чем самые прочные творения рук человеческих. Одна из таких традиций, зародившаяся, по их словам, со времен Первого императора, разворачивается у него на глазах.

Наконец, золотой павильон открылся, явив первозданный облик его сеньора. Все они почтительно поклонились последнему человеку. Его Величество встал и спокойно вышел вперед, держа в руках старую бумагу, прежде чем развернуть ее и произнести простое обращение. Его язык говорил на древнем языке, которого никто из них не понимал, но послание было ясным: поддержите меня, и мы снова принесем мир на острова.

title: RAD_EA.4.t
desc:
Tolfo knew the words to heart.

"Ang bayan ko'y tanging ikaw, Pilipinas kong mahal..."

Nanay sang them to him when he was young. Her sweet dolcetto voice always calmed him down after a tantrum. When Tolfo asked her what the words meant years later, however, she simply gave him a sheepish smile and shrugged her shoulders. Family tradition, he eventually learned, passed to Nanay from Lola and from Lola's Lola and so on.

"Ang puso ko at buhay man, sa iyo'y ibibigay..."

What was a "Pilipinas", anyhow? Was it a place from the Old Times? Was it an idea people used to rally around? Where did it come from? The lyrics would have answered his questions, he was certain. Now if only he knew how to translate a dead language...

"...Ang laya mo'y babantayan..."

As the song on the radio drew to a close, Tolfo let his thoughts wander astray. Its lyrics flew like a majestic bird in his mind's eye, speeding up and slowing down and rising and falling to the beat and tone. It made loops and twirls across the blue sky. It flapped mightily, tossing gusts that blew dust clouds below. In his mind, the bird felt free as it flew. Just as he felt free when he listened to this old lullaby.

With a smile, Tolfo sang the last line of the song he did and did not understand.

title: RAD_EA.6.t
desc:
In the lush and fertile valleys of the Arkan peninsula, a silent battle was waged: one that had clearly been won already. The people native to these lands were sparse, their populations disunited and split apart across various settlements, some at great distances from their fellows. Despite the sparsity of their settlement in the region, it had been their home for millennia. Since the early days of the old world this had remained unchanged.

Until, that is, the new world laid claim to their home.

Vast populations of a previously unknown people flooded into the fertile coastal lands in search of a new home - and a new home was what they found. They arrived in such numbers that they quickly came to dwarf the local population. Simply referred to as "The Outsiders" by the locals, their strange culture rapidly hold of the lands. Within a brief matter of time, entire cities had been established by these people, as the vast fertile lands began to be cultivated by their farmers.

Within the blink of an eye, a civilization all but alien to the locals had popped into existence. Yet as this civilization of the new world rose, so too did their own fall.

title: RAD_EA.7.t
desc:
As the fallout faded, the people of the east would stagger back to their feet. Much had been lost, but all had a chance to begin again, and new societies and cultures would rise in the ashes of the old lands. Innovations were reclaimed or reconceived, art and commerce flourished, and empires would rise. And when the people were once more sufficiently numerous, Pestilence would resume his walk amongst them.

It would begin in the southern jungles. Men would fall sick and feverish, dying horribly days later from open lesions that would not cease bleeding no matter what. By the time those further up the trade route heard the terrible tales, they too would already have fallen ill. Before anyone realized what was happening, the disease spread far and wide. People lay dying in their homes, at their businesses, in the streets. Even Nihon and the distant Indus did not escape the wrath of the plague, burning through urban and rural climes, through rich and poor alike. It would come to be known as the Red Silence, and to all the nations it was as if the world was coming undone once again.

And just as quickly as it came, the Silence would fade away. The dead would be given their due respects where possible, and once more society would rebuild. And this time the destruction was not absolute, for disease can kill a nation's populace but it might leave untouched the nation's institutions. For a time, food would be numerous, wealth would be redistributed, and even the common serf would find himself time to stop, sit and consider his place in the world. And in its contemplation, man would bring forth a new era of thinking. A new wealth of ideas, innovations, and beliefs would invigorate every layer of society. A time of renewal. Of regrowth.

A rebirth.

title: RAD_EA.8.t
desc:
In the early hours of the morning, a boy named Lam-ang stepped foot outside his tribe's land for the first time. With nothing but the clothes on his person and the sack on his back, he ventured a great distance along winding paths of stone -- just as the elder instructed.

Lam-ang's tribe was one of many hundreds scattered across the Seven Thousand Isles. They had their own memories that run far before the day Kaptan had struck the Old World in His righteous anger. As the blue sky flashed orange and thunder clapped where there were no clouds, searing heat torched the barriers that had kept old grudges at bay. Countless moons had passed since the Kamatayan brought the past to an end, yet the peoples that now live atop its corpse seemed insistent on bringing its dead conflicts with them.

With the need to wage war comes the need for food and weapons, and with the need for food and weapons comes the need for strong men. For Lam-ang's tribe, only the strongest would suffice, and so the elder decreed: any boy who wishes to become a man must first journey to the Karaang Gubat and retrieve a relic of the elder's choosing. Only when he returns with it will the elder acknowledge him as a man of the tribe. Lam-ang was tasked to find a banner of blue and red, with yellow stars on a field of white.

Eventually, after traversing hills and streams and dense brush, he finally found the Matandang Gubat. None of the songs prepared Lam-ang for the sight before him: what he thought was an old village was instead tall pillars of stone and metal as far as the eye can see. Brushing aside the last vestiges of fear and doubt, the boy began the arduous task of finding the proof of his manhood among the ruins his ancestors had left behind.

title: RAD_EA.9.t
desc:
It is dawn when the two rouse on the hillside hut, the Old Man and the young child. She giggles as she pokes the slumbering man in his tattered coat - she sometimes counts the rusting badges on it, and loses count by the time she gets to seven. The Old Man is grouchy in the manner of all convalescent elderly, but there is work to be done: the tea-stand must be set up, the leaves and water boiled to the right temperature, the banner unfurled.

When the young girl is bored with the Old Man's calls to clean this or that, she sneaks off, as she is wont to do, into the woods. Once or twice she has found great silvery rust-red machines in the wilderness, with faded insignia on them in blood-red and white. But what they were meant to build or destroy she cannot tell. Today she finds nothing, so she heads to a clearing on the edge of a hill: there she has found something new to watch.

There is a great space in the plain below, and on it lies a tangle of twisted white and grey stone and metal stretching in all directions, rectangular and messy. Traces of jagged stone still show in places in the ruins, and the roads still retain their blackness. In the skyline there are one or two jagged fingers, and the girl likes to imagine that she is there, in the fingers' vast spaces, touching the sky and flying in the great-wings the Old Man tells her about when he is drunk. But the plain of scrambled-wreckage never comes to life, and she heads home at dusk. Whatever this once was, it is dead as picked-clean bones now.

She passes a road sign as she returns on the broken road, fingers the sign's strange pattern, and wonders what Y K HAM 25 KM means. Perhaps the Gods meant it to be a ritual, or perhaps a magic phrase? She shrugs and continues on her way. It is none of her business, and the hearthfire of home awaits - there is nothing for her here.

title: RAD_EA.10.t
desc:
Ishiguro had thought long and hard about how to approach the Lordship for funding. This was, as with all such endeavors, a risky proposition at its core. All remembered the stories of impassable winds, dangerous demon-weapons from the Old World, and natives who disappeared into the jungle to return at night bearing sharp fangs and sharper knives the Teachers had taught them. The monks whispered that the creatures on the other side of the sea had barely been human in the first place - what was the point of trading with near-animals?

He settled upon the creative use of mythology to persuade the Lordship of the expedition's importance. With the merchants he had agreed to pool funds with, Miyazaka and Mitsu, the young merchant appeared at the Province Court with a set of very expensive scrolls. All were pre-War, and all were written in the strange flowing set of characters whose interpretation had been lost to time. Some suspected it had something to do with the strange shapings of names in the tongues of the land, and how some namings with the same meanings were said in entirely different ways in court or marketplace. This was Ishiguro's lead: the Lordship was many things, but above all he was curious.

The Lordship listened patiently to the merchants' promise to return not just with wealth, but with the keys to understanding where the Forgotten Words had come from - and the power that came with reclaiming forgotten names. He agreed to fund the provisioning and the armaments for a convoy of five ships, to be sent to the lands beyond the Southern Diamond.

Months passed. Ishiguro now sat on the deck, watching the emerald landline in the distance grow ever closer. Details magnified and clarified, and became rivers and mountains and the sparkle of life. Ishiguro prepared the scrolls of calligraphy, a few trade goods from the sculpting and crafting centres of the Central Island, and set off with a few soldiers of the Guard on a little boat, to the shores of the Land of Blood and Gold. Chuugoku awaited, and with it the promise of reclaiming lost memory.

Months passed. Ishiguro now sat on the deck, watching the emerald landline in the distance grow ever closer. Details magnified and clarified, and became rivers and mountains and the sparkle of life. Ishiguro prepared the scrolls of calligraphy, a few trade goods from the sculpting and crafting centres of the Central Island, and set off with a few soldiers of the Guard on a little boat, to the shores of the Land of Blood and Gold. Chuugoku awaited, and with it the promise of reclaiming lost memory.

title: RAD_EA.11.t
desc:
As civilization crawled out of the ashes of its own hubris, that which had been made myth was slowly brought back into the light by wise men seeking the betterment of man. Iron horses that rode under the power of steam, great steel birds that could carry men to the skies, hulks of copper wiring that could be tricked into thinking - sufficiently comprehensible magic slowly parsed themselves back into technological theory, and then into reassuring fact, after countless generations of ignorance.

It was in the bay of Narasakai that the men of the New World discovered once more the methods of breaking apart the most fundamental building blocks of the universe, and wielding the unimaginable energy contained within. The mood of the men of the great institute was ecstatic as their Divine Heart came alive, its essence sustained by a carefully choreographed disintegration of the elements. The power contained within was comparable to that of the gods, enough to sustain the entire realm perhaps, enough to usher in a new golden era of peace, knowledge and progress for a thousand years and more.

As the men cheered, an almost imperceptible chill came over one of the researchers. An ancient, unbidden ancestral memory of a power that promised peace but brought only suffering unto untold ages. The man shuddered at the implication of the power that mortals had now been granted. Could men be trusted with the power of divinity? Did they even deserve it? And even if they did, would they use it wisely?

And yet where there was fear, there remained great hope. Hope for not just the islands that were their home, but for every man, woman and child of the earth. If one Heart could be made, then others would surely follow, and the world would awaken to an age without want or scarcity. The dark era of the past no longer haunted the minds of men, and under the sunrise of a man-made star, they might finally know peace.

title: RAD_EA.12.t
desc:
On a clear winter's day, bordering on the cusp of spring, the villager making the arduous hike out of the sheltered valley of Hakone towards the ash plains of Gotemba took a moment's rest while gazing at the mountain beyond, towering above its barren surroundings. The slopes were covered by pockmark-like craters, while the eastward edge suddenly caved away close to the peak, as if a giant had taken a jagged bite out of the mountain itself. The pristine snow capping the summit accentuated the wounds gouged into the mountain against the cloudless sky.

The shrine priests had said ruefully that the mountain was the broken spirit of their ancestors, the Japanese, before the spears of light and flame had fallen from the sky, turning night into brilliant day and then an even longer twilight. Presumably, the spears had also defaced the mountain, scarring the spirit of the ancestors in the priests' legends and myths.

From time to time, the villager would wonder what the mountain and world looked like when both were still whole. Relics of that time could be found just beneath the surface of the ash plains: a broken blade here, a cylindrical metal skeleton there, or the husk of a treaded iron tortoise, asleep in the soil. Many would bear a set of characters that the priests translated as "IMPERIAL JAPANESE ARMY, TAKIGAHARA GARRISON."

The villager shuddered. Despite its utopian abundance, the world that came before didn't seem to be a particularly enviable one, if its inhabitants devoted so much time and energy to killing each other. How perfect could the spirit of a people so consumed by war actually be?

No, the mountain was what it had always been. If it was the spirit of the villager's ancestors (and by extension, the villager himself), then any mention of scars or brokenness rang hollow. It was certainly not flawless - the giant's bite was too obviously unnatural - but it had weathered what terrible cataclysm that had annihilated his ancestors. Where only rusting relics bore witness to the warlike hubris of generations past, the mountain continued its stark repose, forever changed by the world's passing but renewed in its wake.

It was a clear winter's day, bordering on the cusp of spring. The villager began the walk down to the ash plains of Gotemba, in the shadow of the imperfect mountain and with the first shoots of new life sprouting beneath his feet.

title: RAD_EA.13.t
desc:
The boy's mother held a tight grip on his hand, so tight he feared it might break. "Hurts, Mama!" he whimpered. She did not respond, instead fearfully darting her eyes towards the surrounding hills. She turned back to the boy, her hands now crushing his in an iron grip. "Run," she said, "Run, and do not stop. Please. Mama loves you very much, love."

Mother embraced son with those words, as ungodly cries in an alien tongue echoed down from the valley slopes. Tears streamed down the mother's face. "W-where?" the boy asked.

"Anywhere! Just run!" she screamed in reply.

The boy did as she asked, and ran as far and fast as his legs could carry his tiny body, up to the crest of the hills above the valley. The boy turned around, wishing to see why his mother was so insistent that he leave. And so he saw.

The voices from the hills had become flesh, flesh and steel and rage. They had descended upon the caravan, ripping babes from the breasts of mothers, gold from the necks of the rich, and life from the mortal coils of men.

The Hill Men had come, and hell followed with them.

title: RAD_EA.14.t
desc:
In the years following the cataclysm, the land that was once called Kanto has grown cold and barren and depressed. The scattered people possess woes beyond counting. Not all of this is a result of the nuclear holocaust. In what was once called Kanto, sits an old port. Long ago, before mankind's folly, this place was an important site for the construction of waterborne vessels; massive constructs of steel which would traverse the world's oceans.

Much of this "naval yard" was destroyed, reduced to molten slag and water vapor when the bombs fell. One ship remained, however. A vast, half-collapsed edifice of steel and jutting cannons, more than 300 meters long, the home of the most brutal warlord to ever disgrace the land.

From the heart of this "City of Steel", as the locals call it, the Kanto Warlord does not so much rule the land as he rapes it. The descendents of former Army and Navy men, the Steel Legion, emerge from the half-shattered ship once in a cycle, to destroy and raze and pillage with abandon.

In the grand scheme of history, this was nothing unusual.

title: RAD_EA.15.t
desc:
The Old Man pressed on through the snow, his feeble frame straining under the punishing wind. He knew not his bearing, for his eyes had long since clouded over. But he would not be deterred before the unseen mountain ahead, a foreboding challenge both physically and mentally, for in his arms he carried the only treasure remaining in the world.

For hours, or days, the Old Man forced himself to carry on. One step, then another, and another, an eternal march to an unknown salvation. Not for him, but for the Boy, cradled by the Old Man's fragile frame against the uncaring elements. The Boy's parents died so that the Boy might live, even if the body of an invalid was all that remained to honor the parents' last wish: the boy must reach the other side of the mountain, through an endless, freezing climb, while seeing nothing but blurs through a wall of snow and hail.

The Old Man wore many layers, but the inexorable cold penetrated through all of them, seeping so deeply into his bones such that any sense of touch became dulled and distant. His legs gave way, and barely felt his body collapse into the snow. He had failed.

In the distance, however, through the furious snowstorm, the Old Man could hear faint footsteps, an unmistakable crunching of snow underfoot. In desperation and with the last strength, the OId Man raised the Boy in his arms, and shouted out, "Please! Take the Boy! Take him over the Mountain!"

After what felt like hours, the Old Man could hear the crunching of snow growing closer. He prayed that they were not those of the rapacious Steel Legion. Icy tears dribbled out from glazed eyes, freezing on the Old Man's face. "Please," he begged. His arms were lightened; the boy was taken. Seeing the white blur of the snowy sky one last time, the old man closed his shrouded eyes, sinking into a warmer darkness.

title: RAD_EA.16.t
desc:
The river down in the south never seemed to stop churning. Merchants, from the cities in the east, would sail and navigate the waters, selling their cheap wares. They told stories of seas that went off into the distance, and of cities built upon the palaces of the gods. They told of godly tools that could hold a river back and create light from dark, and move a ship without the use of sails.

Xue was an inquisitive boy. When his friends turned their back to go play with junk and his parents went off to work in the fields, Xue would ply travelers for their stories until they finally broke and spilled their tales. Often, they would be mundane. A friend they knew disappeared in the sea to the east, or they knew someone who knew someone who had seen terrible things in the old palaces. The usual old stuff. Occasionally, however, Xue would hear someone talk of the west, and of the empires unknown, and of men with five eyes and four fingers. He would lean in on the edge of his seat to hear those tales, and those nights, he would never get any sleep. His mind wandered endlessly. What lay beyond the hills, to the west?

One particular day, a traveler came from a direction Xue had never seen a traveler come from. Over the mountains and the wall, from the west. His skin was dark, like he had rubbed charcoal over himself. His clothes were tattered. In a broken Putonghua, Xue gathered that he had been separated from a caravan. He brought the man back to his family's cottage, where his family took him in, feeding him until his cheeks were no longer hollow and mending his strange clothes. As he rested, Xue began asking him a torrent of questions. Where was he from, who did he travel with, and what laid in the west? The man gave simple answers. He came from a great desert, over the mountains and on a road thousands of li long. Xue was fascinated, and the man was happy to oblige him.

Eventually, of course, the man had to leave. Xue begged and pleaded with his parents to let him go with him, but they needed their son on the field. When the time came for him to leave, Xue snuck out of the house and followed him down the side of the trail, hiding in the trees. When he was far away enough from the house, he made his presence known. The traveler was not surprised; adolescence had instilled foolish actions in him, too, when he was Xue's age. Nevertheless, he was not one to turn down such a boy, and let him follow along. The father awoke that morning see his son's bed empty. He knew where Xue had gone, and the family mourned. Even if he was not dead, he was as well as such.

The boy, on the long road over the mountains, witnessed palaces of the gods of an unimaginable size. Each new town and each caravan held stories teeming with life. He could not travel to every place, but at least he could hear of them and their people, the horizons offering a clue of what lay over.

title: RAD_EA.17.t
desc:
Another day, another mission the islanders impose on themselves, to save a few poor souls. Ever since the great explosions on the Big Seven, the islands unfortunate enough to be attacked by a mysterious force, the heroic crew had done nothing but work night and day for the good of the archipelago.

The job was simple. The journey began from the base, and the small fleet of wooden rafts based on traditional designs set sail before the sun rose. It was not hard to make them, although by the time resources got scarcer. Navigation techniques were well-known; they were spread in the Ocean millennia before everything changed, and the great explosions would not change that. Once they headed out into the sea, they simply had to reach an island and rescue as many people to bring to the safe havens they resided in. However, this day was different.

All the crew was tired as they approached one of the Big Seven. Sweat ran down their bodies, and waves crashed on the small boat. The weather was bad, real bad. It was not a good way to launch the largest operation yet, a rescue mission in one of the Big Seven themselves. Despite that, the sailors continued, and reached the coast by the afternoon. For hours and into the night, they would work endlessly, with their goal to evacuate as many civilians as possible. They boarded the large rafts made for them in panic, and screams could be heard as they fled the smoldering ruins, battling to get on the boats first.

But the boats were not enough. The island was big, and before the fires the foreigners had made it into a bustling town, one that could not be carried across the waters of the sea. The locals who were not quick enough broke into tears as the boats departed, with the captains making vague promises to return. But they never did. The island remained in isolation for centuries, and no one would be coming to save them.
